methods: All51 source-bound decisions, complete exposed occurrences/raw KG entries, source counts and preserved native rows inspected, not sampled.
Independent chemical/form/product skepticism compares frozen raw labels and complete recipe context to captured primary recipe/supplier/ontology evidence; primary authorship is separate.
All10 original and11 final full proposed owner payloads examined; exact existing-owner deltas checked against original before bytes; source-provenance and formulation-boundary revisions re-reviewed.
Gitignore-independent Path.rglob scan of all maintained YAML checks proposed-new identifier collisions; this is not global ontology absence proof.

All180 final evidence references hash-checked, every original case digest/occurrence ID/backlink verified, all11 final payloads pass native closed-schema validation, entire maintained-catalog overlay passes native component-partonomy.
limitations: This source-case scientific review accepts bounded proposal assertions and retained holds; it does not grant whole-published-owner or SSSOM release approval. All preserved WITHHOLD/REJECTED/role and source-material boundaries remain.
Existing proposed owner payloads preserve inherited assertions, including unrelated role/raw-label/structure concerns; coordinator native complete-owner review remains required before release.
Sodium nicotinate exact-form ontology search is bounded; the CAS-primary candidate explicitly requires renewed exact-term lookup before integration. No global absence is asserted.
Some primary endpoints failed or showed application shells; unsuccessful captures are not positive identity evidence. Source snapshots are context, not independent chemical proof.
No maintained data, downstream outputs, GitHub issues, commits or external sessions were changed by this independent reviewer.

case_reviews.appraisal: TOGO M2313 places brown-algae laminarin among alternative 0.2% carbon sources. CHEBI:6364 describes the polymer class, while the current owner explicitly claims Laminaria digitata. The source does not establish that species, so retaining the broader interpretation and withholding the narrower alias is justified.

JCM393 explicitly names sodium nicotinate at0.725g; NIST supports CAS54-86-4 and C6H4NNaO2. The proposed CAS owner preserves the sodium salt and uses NARROW_MATCH to the nicotinic-acid parent rather than an exact acid identity. The exact salt-term search is bounded and must remain a documented integration limitation; absence of a term is not established by this review. A separate independent lookup checked ChEBI255 and NCIt26.02d exact CAS/name variants and found no matching salt term within those bounded stores; the captured false positives are unrelated.

DSMZ1894 ingredient2443 is20g supermarket soya flour. FoodOn soybean-flour scope and the existing Soy_Flour owner fit this raw spelling. A same-material alias is justified without assigning processing grade, catalog identity, or molecular composition. The matching KG case remains a separate observation.

The TOGO M2844 comment makes0.2N KOH a constituent solvent for the bromothymol-blue preparation. It is not an exact synonym of pure KOH or an independent5g/L material; the legacy flattened quantity must not migrate into a molecular owner.

The Ethane occurrence is a gas constituent in the TOGO M1198/JCM1120 context. CHEBI:42266 is the exact C2H6 molecule. The new molecular owner adds no assertion that the full gas phase, specified gas dose, or stock equals ethane; source and live-fetch limitations are disclosed.

Both frozen NBRC contexts explicitly name Nalidixic acid inside antibiotic stocks with different concentrations. CHEBI:100147 represents the free acid, distinct from the existing sodium-salt owner. The proposed molecular owner leaves stock solvent, stock identity and final-medium dose unasserted.

JCM1385 points its VFA component to JCM1130, which names isovaleric and n-valeric separately. The space variant iso -Valeric acid denotes branched CHEBI:28484, not the linear acid. The raw alias has source-specific provenance and does not absorb the whole VFA stock.

JCM600 specifies an aqueous toluene preparation and a40mL addition. The source label5mM/water-saturated describes preparation context; the frozen40g quantity is not chemically validated. A pure-toluene synonym would lose solvent and concentration scope, so no such edit is supported.

DSMZ672 permits Difco0003 OR0001 nutrient broth at half concentration. The explicit alternative must not become one product identity or a universal nutrient-broth alias. Product/version and prepared concentration remain necessary for any whole-mixture owner.

All five n--Valeric acid occurrences are read in their VFA source contexts. Primary VFA recipes distinguish linear from branched acid; CHEBI:17418 supports the linear molecule. The proposed spelling alias does not approve legacy mass units or flatten the VFA stock.

The NBRC context uses29.5g/L commercial BBL fluid-thioglycolate medium plus separately added sodium thioglycolate. A supplier contrast for a different product does not prove the exact BBL catalog formula. Keeping the commercial medium distinct from thioglycolate and deferring exact product identity is justified.

All five iso--Valeric acid occurrences retain the branched-acid interpretation in their VFA contexts. CHEBI:28484 and primary JCM VFA naming distinguish it from n-valeric acid. The raw spelling alias is supported while inherited quantity errors remain outside the proposal.

The3FEBA occurrence is R2A liquid medium at1FOLD. Current R2A agar identity cannot be substituted without proving agar inclusion; a separate supplier broth formula is comparative evidence only. The retained formulation/form hold is scientifically specific.

TOGO M2972 supplies1000mL of R2A(Difco), which is a prepared product reference without enough agar/formulation/version detail. Neither pure ingredient nor automatic R2A-agar identity follows from the label. The exact product preparation remains unresolved.

NBRC19 names2g peptic pepton(USB) but the captured record does not identify an exact catalog or digestion substrate. That is insufficient to equate the product to a generic animal/soy peptone owner. The hold preserves the product-level distinction.

DSMZ88's modified recipe adds20g sulfide ore. A pyrite example does not define all ore constituents or establish FeS2 as exact whole-material identity. Mineral composition/source is a real unresolved requirement, not a synonym formatting task.

Both SONG/MediaDB288 and289 occurrences expressly retain unavailable amounts and withdraw the prior VARIABLE default. The corrected decision preserves missing dose as missing. CHEBI:17013 identifies the nucleotide concept, but supplied counterion and reagent form remain unproved; no exact free-acid owner is asserted.

The NBRC1488/TOGO M2143 glycine-betaine label and supplier/ontology evidence support the neutral zwitterion CHEBI:17750. The proposed owner remains distinct from existing hydrochloride and hydrate records. The source dose is not transferred as a universal property.

The primary Denger/Cook study explicitly concerns R/S sulfolactate use, which does not justify selecting a single S-form owner from the unspecific source heading. Reagent salt, stereochemical mixture and experimental-condition selection require methods-level resolution; the hold is warranted.

JCM1385 directs n -Valeric acid to JCM1130's VFA formulation. The linear pentanoic acid identity is supported independently by CHEBI:17418; whitespace normalization is safe at molecule scope and does not imply whole-stock identity.

Trimethylglycine in10NLDM is a separate occurrence of the glycine-betaine zwitterion supported by ontology and supplier synonyms. Sharing the proposed CHEBI:17750 owner is justified; the source's attached ontology enrichment alone is not treated as independent proof.

NBRC957/1045 identify30g BBL Trypticase Soy broth and separately handle agar. The product is a multi-component medium, not trypticase peptone alone. An exact catalog/version formula has not been established, so the whole-product hold is justified.

JCM906 supplies100mL of a0.5M glycine/NaOH pH10 buffer. Pure glycine would omit titrant and stock scope; the legacy100g unit is not approved. The source does not allocate NaOH amount, so no exact quantitative whole-buffer composition is invented.

The CCAP grass-media contexts use cereal-grass leaves/extract, including distinct recipes and amounts. Leaves are not grain flour, and the source gives no unique plant species. No wheat-flour or species-specific grass identity is inferred.

All nine Methane gas occurrences denote CH4 as a gas component; CHEBI:16183 verifies the molecule. The new raw alias preserves all rejected produces-methane trait labels and does not identify a mixed headspace as pure methane. Dose and atmosphere assertions are outside this alias proposal.

NBRC1394 resolves the misspelled PQQ name and shows1mg/L, while the frozen1g/L is a thousandfold discrepancy. PQQ concept recognition does not settle supplied salt or permit the incorrect dose. The proposal correctly stops short of inventing a free-acid owner or endorsing the quantity.

The exact nested P5/MEM stock occurrence explicitly specifies L-Asparagine*H2O. Sigma A8381 documentation supports L-asparagine monohydrate CAS5794-13-8. The alias preserves both L configuration and hydration and does not merge with DL hydrate or anhydrous asparagine; stock concentration stays source-scoped.

The archived DSM560 context specifies methanethiol gas, and CHEBI:16007 is the exact CH4S molecule. Failed live retrieval is honestly recorded. The new owner is a molecular identity proposal only; the1–2mL/50mL preparation is not converted into an unsupported mass concentration.

MediaDive2119's6-methylnicotinate label does not distinguish acid, anion/salt or ester. Its automated CAS5470-70-2 conflicts with TCI's methyl ester formula, so automatic enrichment is not an identity witness. Retaining the unresolved owner and seeking the actual reagent is justified.

MediaDive298 names Na-stearate and the exact sodium-octadecanoate concept CHEBI:132109 fits. The label already exists on the current owner, so an empty proposal is appropriate. The prior complete-alias WITHHOLD remains in force; source-name agreement does not approve the exported row.

proposal_reviews.appraisal: Accept the two source spelling aliases for linear valeric acid. Exact after payload preserves all preexisting fields and assertions, adds only aliases plus curation history, and supplies primary recipe/ontology source provenance. Existing pentanoate/role/raw-label concerns are not newly approved.

Accept the two branched-acid spelling aliases. JCM primary recipe distinguishes branched from linear acid; provenance was refined in v3. Existing chemistry and unrelated inherited aliases/roles remain untouched and require coordinator whole-payload review before release.
Accept Methane gas at molecular CH4 scope. Exact payload preserves both REJECTED_LABEL trait entries and all earlier assertions, and adds no gas-mixture, headspace dose or role claim.

Accept Soya flour for the existing soybean-flour category using the source2443/DSMZ1894 bridge. Two source cases share a spelling proposal without an occurrence-count merge. No grade or supplier-product formulation is invented.

Accept the explicitly L/monohydrate alias on CAS5794-13-8 only. Supplier identity verifies this form. The proposal preserves the existing parent relation and does not validate inherited stereochemically underspecified structure strings or replace them with a new assertion.

Accept source-bound new C2H6 molecular identity CHEBI:42266 as an isolated proposal. No duplicate maintained primary identifier was found in a gitignore-independent data/ingredients scan. No whole gas phase or concentration mapping is proposed.

Accept the exact nalidixic-acid molecular owner CHEBI:100147, distinct from sodium salt and source antibiotic stocks. Minimal payload has direct ontology evidence, source labels and curation audit; it does not claim that the stock is pure free acid.

Accept shared glycine-betaine/trimethylglycine zwitterion CHEBI:17750 owner. Both source cases support this molecule; existing hydrochloride and hydrate stay separate. No roles or solution quantities are imported.

Accept CH4S methanethiol CHEBI:16007 as a distinct molecular proposal based on the primary term and frozen gas-source context. Live recipe retrieval failure is retained; dose conversions and mixture identity are not asserted.

Accept CAS-preserved sodium salt as a conditional integration candidate with NARROW_MATCH parent, never exact acid identity. Bounded search does not prove no salt-specific ontology term; the record itself requires renewed exact-term lookup before integration. No parent-role or whole stock approval follows. Independent versioned local ChEBI/NCIt lookup now supplies bounded negative evidence; global ontology absence is still not claimed.
